problem_text:
A logistics company must devise a procurement and storage strategy for a critical component across an 18-day operational window.  
The initial stockpile at the start of the planning interval is 71 units.  
For each day \( t = 1, \dots, 18 \), the vendor permits the company to issue a procurement request, with the quantity required to fall between 4 and 61 units.  
Each such request, however, incurs a lead time of 1 day before the units become available for fulfilling requirements or augmenting the stock.  
The daily requirement for the component is specified as:  
Day 1: 11 units  
Day 2: 13 units  
Day 3: 48 units  
Day 4: 60 units  
Day 5: 35 units  
Day 6: 18 units  
Day 7: 45 units  
Day 8: 56 units  
Day 9: 55 units  
Day 10: 29 units  
Day 11: 36 units  
Day 12: 35 units  
Day 13: 44 units  
Day 14: 13 units  
Day 15: 57 units  
Day 16: 38 units  
Day 17: 44 units  
Day 18: 19 units  

Deficits are permissible, but any unsatisfied requirement is simply lost and not carried forward.  
Throughout the 18-day horizon, component quantities may be treated as continuous values, and the total physical stock held at any moment must not surpass the storage facility’s limit of 71 units.  
The aggregate expense comprises three elements: a procurement cost of 5 per unit acquired; a storage cost of 1 per unit held overnight; and a deficit penalty of 7 per unit of unmet daily requirement.  
The objective is to establish the optimal acquisition quantity for each day and to monitor the ensuing stock and deficit levels so as to minimize the total expenditure.
